heroHeadline: 'Project Freedom' Launches at Hormuz: US Military Begins Escorting Ships as Iran Claims It Blocked Navy; Lebanon Ceasefire Monitoring Mechanism Strained by Daily Israeli Strikes
heroSubtitle: The US launched 'Project Freedom' on May 4, 2026 — deploying guided-missile destroyers, 100+ aircraft, and 15,000 service members to escort commercial vessels through the Strait of Hormuz after Trump rejected Iran's comprehensive 14-point peace proposal as 'unacceptable.' Iran's IRGC simultaneously claimed it had 'prevented US Navy ships from entering the Strait,' creating a direct maritime confrontation risk that effectively suspends the diplomatic track maintained through Pakistan. The launch comes after three successive rejected Iranian proposals since May 1. On the Lebanon track, Lebanese Army Chief Gen. Haykal and US General Clearfield held two 'exceptional' military coordination meetings in 48 hours (May 2–3) at the Beirut air base, attempting to salvage the monitoring mechanism as the IDF struck 50+ Hezbollah sites on May 2 and 70+ structures on May 3 — with IDF Chief Zamir continuing to state there is 'no ceasefire' in south Lebanon. Hezbollah issued five conditions for the ceasefire to hold, including full Israeli withdrawal and no direct Lebanon-Israel negotiations. The three-week ceasefire extension runs nominally to approximately May 14 with no diplomatic breakthrough expected. Ten ceasefire frameworks remain technically in force globally, but the US-Iran and Lebanon-Israel tracks are both in acute crisis simultaneously — making this the most concentrated test of global peace architecture since the framework's January 2026 ceasefire phase began.
